The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=2,$ the particle is located at the position $x=8.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=7?$

The position of the particle at $t=7$ is $x=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=7$ is equal to its position at $t=2$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [2,7].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(7)=x(2)+{\int }_{2}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(2)=8$, and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{2}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=2$ to $t=7.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{2}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t=-3.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(7)=8+(-3)=5.
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=7$ is $x=5.$
